description.purpose: The drain's own bookkeeping, and nothing else: one table with two kinds of row. A 'batch' row is the closed day parked between two hops (the script keeps no state, so the conversation has to survive the ledger read it triggers); a 'mark' row says how far this session has reached the memory hive. That number is the whole dedup guarantee - it is read BEFORE anything is written, and it is what makes a second delivery of the same batch a skip instead of a double insert.
description.use_when: One per memory-drain hive. Nothing else writes here, and the drain reads nothing else: the hive's episodes table is not this store's business and is never touched from here.
description.not_in_scope: No memory, no episodes, no extraction, no retrieval. The parked day is a transport buffer, not a second record of the conversation - the durable record is the episodes table of the memory hive, and the window store of the talky before it. No cross-session reads: every op is scoped by session_id.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result per op. hop.operation drives the drain's phase machine (insert -> select -> insert), hop.rows_affected is the store's own count. hop.duration_ms is what that reply cost in milliseconds. A bundle reply (two or more tool_call turns, GH #295) stamps hop.operation 'bundle', sums hop.rows_affected over its legs and adds hop.bundle_errors: how many legs carry an error_code. That key is present on every bundle reply, 0 included, and never on a single-operation reply -- it is what an edge reads to see that one leg failed without opening the body, while hop.error_code keeps its hard meaning (the WHOLE reply is a refusal). results[]: the per-operation metadata of that same bundle reply, one entry per leg in call order -- {tool_call_id, operation, rows_affected, duration_ms} plus error_code if that one leg failed. It is a top-level body slot and not a key on the turn because a tool_result turn stays schema-pure ({origin, type, text, id}; ubf-body.json $defs/TurnObject is additionalProperties:false, so a metadata key there would dead-letter the whole reply), and tool_call_id is what ties an entry back to its turn. Like bundle_errors the slot exists only on a bundle reply -- a single-operation reply carries messages[] alone.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: tool_call turns with store-native args. The lane a reply belongs to is carried by context.drain_origin ('drain'), the step by context.drain_phase, both promoted by the internal edge that sent the op.
examples: {operation: insert, table: drain_log, row: {id, session_id, kind: 'batch', payload: <the day as json>, drained_upto: 0, recorded_at}} -> the day survives the read it is about to trigger

{operation: select, table: drain_log, columns: [id, kind, payload, drained_upto], where: {session_id}, order_by: [{col: 'id', dir: 'asc'}]} -> the newest parked day and every mark of the session in ONE reply
{operation: insert, table: drain_log, row: {kind: 'mark', drained_upto: 6, ...}} -> six turns of this session are in the memory hive under the ids s#0..s#5
